messages:
Jen (support): Hey team, BrightCart is seeing sustained 429s during a 30m burst this morning. They say Dedicated pool isn't scaling up fast enough — requests queue and we hit their client-side timeouts. They provided timeline and a quick repro.

Maya (oncall): Got the ticket. Any immediate logs or sample request IDs?

Jen (support): Pasting the customer's repro steps and a snippet of our ingress errors. They reproduce with a 1500 rps spike for ~4m. Example error from our edge: `error=429 resource=dedicated/attach_queue`

Jen (support): Customer repro steps (condensed):
1) Send burst: 1500 concurrent /v1/generate requests with seq len 512
2) Observe ~30% 429s after 45s into the burst
3) After traffic drops, it takes ~2m for pods to be marked Ready and traffic to drain

Tom (eng-runtime): Can you dump the autoscaler events and warm-pool state? My suspicion: probe failures + cold KV cache causing longer init latency per replica.

Ali (eng-platform): On it — checking cluster events and min/max config for that account. Also verifying imagePull status and node pressure.

ops-bot: [autoscaler] detected surge for acct=brightcart, desired_replicas=40, current_replicas=12, min_replicas=10, max_replicas=50, cooldown=45s

Jen (support): Customer's config: min_replicas=10, max_replicas=50, burst_policy=aggressive, prewarm=false. They expected faster spin-up because their SLA says reserved throughput.

Maya (oncall): I pulled the autoscaler events. There are repeated `scale up triggered` events but `AttachQueue` backlog shows steady growth. Events show `scale decision delayed: probe_timeout` a few times around 3932100450.

Tom (eng-runtime): Paste of recent pod startup logs (truncated):
```
[2026-05-14T10:12:22Z] pod/rc-72 start init
[2026-05-14T10:12:23Z] downloading model shards... ok
[2026-05-14T10:12:45Z] kv-cache-restore: miss
[2026-05-14T10:13:05Z] runtime ready, serving endpoints
[2026-05-14T10:13:07Z] health-check failed (startup-probe) - retrying
[2026-05-14T10:13:25Z] health-check passed
```
Tom (eng-runtime): So each pod has a variable ~20-30s additional delay due to kv-cache miss and startup probe flakiness. That stacks across replicas during a large burst.

Ali (eng-platform): Cluster view: imagePulls fine, no node OOM. But I see kube-scheduler backpressure at 3932100502 — a transient shortage of ephemeral ports on a subset of nodes (noisy tenant). Also one node had slow kubelet heartbeats for ~60s.

Liz (customer-success): Customer extremely sensitive to 429s; they're on Dedicated reserved plan expecting near-zero throttling for that capacity. They're pushing for a postmortem and mitigation asap.

Maya (oncall): Hypothesis: a combination of (a) autoscaler cooldown + attach queue pacing, (b) startup-probe retries when kv-cache cold, and (c) noisy neighbor causing scheduling jitter. Together they push effective spin-up from ~8s to ~45-90s per pod.

Jen (support): I captured `kubectl get pods` snapshot during the incident:```
NAME                 READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
rc-72-abcde          1/1     Running   0          2m
rc-72-fghij          0/1     Init      0          40s
rc-72-klmno          0/1     ContainerCreating 0   38s
```

Tom (eng-runtime): Short-term mitigations:
- Increase `min_replicas` for their pool to cover expected burst (auto-booking?)
- Enable `prewarm=true` for critical customers to keep KV cache hot
- Reduce startup probe strictness to avoid retries that block readiness

Ali (eng-platform): Platform options:
- Fast path: temporarily bump reserved nodes for BrightCart for next 24h while we triage
- Medium: adjust autoscaler aggressiveness and reduce cooldown for reserved pools (ask SRE)
- Long: implement warm-pool with warmed KV snapshots seeded to reduce cold miss penalty

deploy-bot: Scheduled a canary change to startup-probe timeout on staging @maya, ping when ready to run canary.

Maya (oncall): I'm running a quick canary to relax startup probe from 10s -> 30s on staging now. Will monitor for regressions.

Jen (support): Customer approved temporary reserved node bump while we run checks. I've logged the billing + account ops ticket for a 24h reserve.

Liz (customer-success): I'll communicate the temporary mitigation and ETA: 2h for reserve change, 4h for canary -> rollout -> verify. I'll also ask customer for sample request IDs to correlate traces.

Tom (eng-runtime): Action items:
- [Tom] instrument per-pod KV restore time and expose metric `kv_restore_seconds` (priority P1)
- [Ali] propose autoscaler config change for reserved pools, include cooldown and aggressive backoff exceptions (P1)
- [Maya] monitor staging canary and promote if green (P0)
- [Jen] apply 24h reserved node bump for BrightCart and record billing impact (P0)

Jen (support): Noted. I'll update ticket and follow up with logs when reserve is active.

Maya (oncall): One more note — we saw one scheduler rejection with `Insufficient ephemeral-ports` from a noisy tenant at 3932100528. Platform should consider port allocation limits per-tenant.

Ali (eng-platform): Filed infra task INF-7812 to look into ephemeral port pressure and noisy-tenant QoS.

Liz (customer-success): Customer thanks everyone, asking for a short writeup after root cause.

Jen (support): I'll keep this thread updated and close once we have RCA + timeline. :white_check_mark:
